source_method: Public institutional, diocesan, official community and current local reports; cite only explicitly supported details. Weiser remains a historical locator, never independent corroboration.

records.french_name: Herbergsuche — dévotion locale de l'hospitalité pendant l'Avent
records.claim: Vienna's Kaiserebersdorf parish documents nine days of voluntary Advent household gatherings, 15–23 December, with prayer, Scripture and the lodging-search song.
records.calendar: Parish programme, 15–23 December in the cited account; not universal Advent scheduling

sources.supports: Eight house groups, historical nine-day model, locally variable practice

limits: Not the Mexican Las Posadas: shared lodging theme is not identical local custom.
Parish schedule in 2018 is not automatically the current or 1962 universal calendar.

records.english_name: La guignolée — French Canadian Christmas alms collection
records.french_name: La guignolée — quête caritative canadienne-française de Noël
records.claim: Quebec's cultural heritage registry attributes the organized 1860s doorstep Christmas food collection to the Catholic Society of St Vincent de Paul; the society's continuing local programme independently records the tradition.
records.calendar: Christmas-season charity drive; actual annual dates locally announced

sources.issuer: Québec Ministry of Culture / Répertoire du patrimoine culturel
sources.supports: Catholic St Vincent de Paul origins in 1860s; food donations and singing; continuing charitable adaptation

sources.issuer: Society of St Vincent de Paul, Montréal
sources.supports: Organized Christmas charity campaign and continuing guignolée

limits: Later nonreligious charitable collections do not automatically retain explicit Catholic religious character.
Do not invent universal collection days, donations or parish participation.

records.french_name: Kolędnicy polonais — quêteurs et chanteurs de Noël
records.claim: Poland's Ministry of Culture documents regional carolling groups, their house visits, songs and gifts, including region-specific costumes and dramatic forms.
records.calendar: Christmas cycle; dates and troupe forms differ across regions

sources.issuer: Polish Ministry of Culture and National Heritage
sources.supports: House-to-house singing, gifts and regional custom variants

limits: Some performances contain secular folklore; not all forms are explicitly Catholic rites.
Do not conflate Polish groups with German Epiphany Sternsinger or Hungarian Bethlehem play.

records.claim: The Diocese of Linz specifically places fruit-tree branches on St Barbara's 4 December observance, kept in water in hope of flowering at Christmas.
records.calendar: Traditional observance 4 December; voluntary domestic symbolism, not a Mass rite

sources.supports: St Barbara, 4 December, traditional Christmas-flowering branches

limits: The natural bloom is horticultural, not a guaranteed divine sign.
Does not establish obligatory plant species or universal liturgical use.

records.english_name: L-Irxoxt — Maltese running procession with the Risen Christ
records.french_name: L-Irxoxt — procession maltaise du Ressuscité portée au pas de course
records.claim: Malta's public administration documents the traditional Easter Sunday L-Irxoxt procession, and contemporary reporting directly witnesses local runs with statues of the risen Christ.
records.geo: Malta and Gozo, confirmed in named communities
records.calendar: Easter Sunday, only parishes with actual announced procession

sources.supports: Traditional L-Irxoxt Resurrection procession as Easter Sunday custom
Observed statue-running in Senglea and Three Cities on Easter Sunday

limits: The government overview supports procession, independent reporting supports running in specific localities.
No procession may be created by the date alone in the 1962 Mass reader.

records.english_name: Faradda di li Candareri — Sassari's Marian offering procession
records.french_name: Faradda di li Candareri — procession votive mariale de Sassari
records.claim: The Sardinian regional heritage portal and the official festival record independently identify the Assumption-eve 14 August procession carrying large wooden symbolic candles in Sassari.
records.calendar: 14 August local procession associated with Assumption, not a universal Marian vigil rite

sources.supports: 14 August Marian procession, votive origin and guild structures
Annual public processional custom and distinct local context

limits: Festival's local procession is not the generic Roman Assumption procession.
Festival website gives conflicting counts of wooden candle structures; do not publish a count until reconciled.
